title: Support telemetry from the sample-agent client - dedicated dialect, route, scope, enablement, tests
summary: The sample-agent client (traces behind a beta flag) emits standard identity attributes but custom token fields and no operation-name attribute, so the generic recognizer claims the payload and the shared gate rejects every span: zero events, zero dead-letter records. This plan adds a dedicated sample_agent dialect that anchors on the request span name, re-sums the client's cache-exclusive input tokens into the canonical cache-inclusive total, wires a dedicated ingest route, registers a hidden-first auth scope, updates the enablement page, and validates end-to-end in a staging environment with a real client session.
verified_facts: A capture spike showed request spans carry a system attribute, a request-model attribute, a response id, finish reasons, plus custom input, output, cache-read and cache-creation token counts.
Input token counts are cache-exclusive: spans show a tiny input value alongside a large cache-read value, so the canonical total must add the two.
Client docs confirm traces are still beta and the default export protocol is gRPC, so the quickstart must force HTTP protobuf.
An upstream request to emit richer spans was closed as not-planned, but a classifier anchored on the request span name still ingests the degraded shape.
The branch is current with the mainline and there is zero prior art for this dialect in the repo; two recent mainline commits are absorbed cleanly.
The canonical total field is cache-inclusive by a type-level invariant, so no schema change and no generated-model regeneration is needed.
assumptions: The operation-name attribute is absent on client spans - inferred from the spike, not yet re-verified against the raw capture. Wave 0 verifies before implementation.
The scope name follows existing precedent for ingest scopes.
The large raw capture is not fetchable through automation; Wave 0 downloads it manually or regenerates a fresh capture locally.

decisions_for_approval.question: Also prepend the new recognizer to the shared generic route chain?
decisions_for_approval.recommendation: No for this change - dedicated route only. A recognizer claims a whole payload, so on the shared route a mixed batch would be claimed by the new dialect and its restrictive span predicate would silently swallow the other spans, recreating the very silent-drop failure this work eliminates. Scope is enforced per route, so a customer holding only the generic scope would get client parsing without ever holding the hidden client scope, bypassing the scope-unhide launch lever.
decisions_for_approval.alternative: File a follow-up for generic-route handling behind explicit sign-off, and note the limitation on the enablement page.

decisions_for_approval.question: How do we satisfy no-silent-drops when a claimed payload yields zero qualifying spans?
decisions_for_approval.recommendation: Emit a drop record with a no-qualifying-spans reason from the adapter when decomposition yields zero units. A code read confirmed the framework yields nothing in that case today, so this step is required, not decorative.
decisions_for_approval.alternative: Accept zero-output batches as normal - rejected, it violates the event-or-dead-letter-never-nothing metric.

decisions_for_approval.question: Map the time-to-first-token field?
decisions_for_approval.recommendation: No for this change - there is no canonical slot and adding one triggers schema regeneration and downstream churn. Note as a follow-up if the product wants latency detail.
decisions_for_approval.alternative: Stash it in the context bag.

waves.name: Wave 0 - Facts and fixture acquisition (blocks everything)

tasks.title: Acquire a real client trace payload
tasks.text: Do both paths. First, manually download the large raw capture from the spike ticket in the browser, because automation cannot fetch attachments. Second, regenerate a fresh capture: run a client session with telemetry enabled, the traces beta flag on, the exporter set to the OTLP protocol, the protocol forced to HTTP protobuf, and the endpoint pointed at a local collector, to get the exact wire shape the ingest function will see. The second path is also the dress rehearsal for the staging end-to-end test.
tasks.output: Raw OTLP JSON captured to the session directory

tasks.title: Verify the load-bearing facts against the raw payload
tasks.text: Confirm the facts the design leans on: (1) verify the operation-name attribute is truly absent on request spans across the whole capture, not just the summarized ones, which decides whether the shared gate could ever pass; (2) verify input token counts are cache-exclusive trace-wide, which decides the re-sum; (3) capture the wire shape - the resource-span structure and the service-name value - which decides the recognizer anchor; (4) check whether any cache-creation split attributes are emitted beyond the plain total, which decides whether the detail field is populated.
tasks.output: Facts appended to the context file; a sanitized fixture drafted

waves.name: Wave 1 - Core dialect and route (one change, dispatched as one sequential blade)

tasks.title: Source enum
tasks.text: Add the client value to the source enumeration.

tasks.title: Parametrize the span-classifier seam
tasks.text: Add a keyword-only span-predicate argument to the shared decomposer with a safe default so existing dialects construct unchanged. Add a predicate that matches the client request span by name and a present request-model attribute; interaction, tool and hook spans are non-events. Add a regression test proving the defaulted argument is behaviorally identical to passing the shared predicate explicitly.

tasks.title: Dialect module
tasks.text: Add the dialect module modeled on an existing one: a layered adapter over the decomposer plus the shared contributors and a token override. The override reads the custom token attributes and builds the canonical total as input plus cache-read plus cache-creation, because client input is cache-exclusive while the canonical total is cache-inclusive. Add a short comment citing the capture evidence and date, since the client flipping input to cache-inclusive mid-beta would turn the re-sum into silent double-counting.

test_plan.unit: Recognizer claim-and-reject matrix, classifier span-type matrix, token re-sum math against the captured numbers, identity mapping, and a validator round-trip.
test_plan.fixture_parity: A real sanitized capture in the fixtures directory plus registry chain-resolution and drift tests.
test_plan.integration: One full pipeline case from raw envelope to canonical event.
test_plan.regression: The entire existing dialect suite stays green with zero edits to its assertions, proving the shared change is additive only.
test_plan.e2e_staging: A real client session to the staging route lands canonical events with the right identity and token totals compared span by span to the capture.
test_plan.silent_drop: A payload with only non-qualifying spans produces a drop record; a client payload on the generic route still silently drops - the accepted, documented limitation.

conventions_contract.note: Injected verbatim into every implementer prompt; the reviewer enforces it.
pattern_fidelity: The dialect module mirrors an existing one exactly: a module docstring, a source constant, private contributor functions, labeled fragment contributors, and a build factory - no novel structure.
The recognizer mirrors an existing cheap structural predicate with an anchor-span constant and no schema parsing in the claim path.
Reuse the shared coercion helpers - never hand-roll attribute extraction.
The new constructor argument is keyword-only with a safe default.
principles: The fail-open contract is inviolable: no exception escapes the ingest path; errors are logged and swallowed.
Changes to shared code are additive only; overrides are appended after the base so merge-order wins are explicit.
Comments only for non-obvious constraints; no narration comments.
No schema changes; if any become necessary, regenerate the generated model in the same commit.
Keep it simple: one dialect, one predicate, one override list; the generalization stays in its follow-up.

risks: Client beta churn on names: span or attribute renames break the recognizer - mitigated by anchoring on the most stable signal, pinning fixtures, and documenting the beta status.

Client beta churn on semantics: input flipping to cache-inclusive mid-beta would make the re-sum double-count silently - mitigated by the evidence comment, an enablement fragility note, and a periodic live spot-check.
Client traffic sent to the generic route still silently drops - the accepted limitation for this change, called out in the quickstart and tracked by a follow-up.
The operation-name attribute might actually be present, which would change the design - Wave 0 kills this risk before code.
Zero-unit drop semantics may need a minimal framework touch behind the client path only.
Cross-team sequencing: the scope must exist and staging must be manually deployed before any end-to-end run - both have bitten before.

estimate.loc_production: About 250 lines across the dialect, the recognizer, the shared seam, the registry, the enum, the template, and the docs.
estimate.loc_tests: About 735 lines across the dialect suite, the fixture, and the registry and integration cases.
estimate.prs: One core change in this repo bundling the dialect, the route, and the drift tests, plus one tiny scope change in the identity repo that can merge first in parallel, plus an enablement-page edit that is not a code change. A single change within this repo is deliberate: the route without the dialect, or the dialect without the drift tests, would each be a broken intermediate state, so they ship together.

how_to_send_otel_from_claude_code.note: Sender-side setup - what a customer, or we during capture and end-to-end runs, must do. Traces are beta and off by default.
steps: Enable telemetry with the telemetry flag.
Enable the traces beta flag, without which no spans exist.
Turn on the traces exporter and set it to the OTLP protocol.
Force HTTP protobuf, because the client default is gRPC which the gateway cannot terminate.
Point the traces-specific endpoint variable at the full route, because the generic endpoint variable appends a different path and misses the route.
Set the auth header to the raw API key with no bearer prefix; the key must hold the client ingest scope.
Run any client session; each turn exports request spans that become canonical events.
gotchas: Forgetting to force HTTP protobuf fails silently at the exporter.
Using the generic endpoint variable sends to the wrong path and returns an auth or not-found error.
Adding a bearer prefix breaks auth - the header value is the raw key.
Do not point the client at the generic route; its spans are silently dropped there - always use the dedicated route.
